newsitem.title: GREECE: Wave of labour strikes threaten to cripple Greece.
newsitem.headline: Wave of labour strikes threaten to cripple Greece.

text.p: A nationwide 24-hour strike by Greece's biggest labour federations crippled public services, transport, schools and hospitals on Thursday, government and union officials said.

The strike was called to protest against the 1997 austerity budget, due to be presented on Friday. National Economy Minister Yannos Papandoniou has said it will be the toughest budget in 15 years as Greece struggles to get in line with other EU states.
Officials said the strike was disrupting air, sea, train and urban transport. There were no buses or trolleys in Athens and few taxis. Ministries were working with reduced staffs.
Workers in the public sector, including state banks, appeared to be following the strike to some extent while workers in the private sector appeared to ignore it.

The General Confederation of Greek Workers (GSEE), Greece's largest public and private sector labour grouping with about three million members, called the walkout to protest against the budget. The union of civil servants (ADEDY) has joined in.

Workers at state-run Olympic Airways staged a three-hour stoppage in the morning, delaying international and domestic flights. Civil aviation employees, except traffic controllers, have called for a three-hour stoppage in the evening.
Farmers held rallies around the country to press for higher price supports and fuel subsidies. They threatened to put up roadblocks on national highways during the day.
GSEE and ADEDY workers marched through central Athens to the national economy ministry and parliament.
The budget includes the abolition of most tax breaks and cuts state spending to meet targets set by the European Union's Maastricht treaty.
Greece is the only EU country that has failed to meet any of the criteria for joining the Economic and Monetary Union (EMU).
The socialist government has said it is determined to push through its austerity budget, incomes policy and tax reforms to close the large gap between Greece and its EU partners.
